title: CS QBR: Modular Dual-Track Slate & Renewal Playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a modular QBR deck template and accompanying renewal playbook aimed to cover both Standard (product/usage-focused) and Enterprise (strategic + technical) customer reviews. The goal is to reduce prep time, unify storylines across CS, Sales, and Solutions, and increase renewal predictability by surfacing risks and commitments early.

Audience:
- Standard: Product managers, PLG users, SMB and mid-market buyers.
- Enterprise: Platform engineering leads, SRE, procurement, legal, executive sponsors.

Approach overview (what makes this different):
- Dual-track: single one-page executive story that splits into two tracks during the meeting: Business/Value (Standard) and Technical/Operational (Enterprise).
- Modular slide blocks: each slide is a reusable block. For each customer, assemble 6–12 blocks for Standard, 10–18 for Enterprise.
- Renewal-first framing: every QBR ends with a clear renewal posture: Green/Amber/Red + top 3 asks and owner commitments.

Quick exec one-pager (always open the meeting with this):
- Title: Customer Name — QBR Snapshot (Quarter, Year)
- 60s TL;DR: adoption highlight + 1 sentence ROI statement
- Net change: key metric deltas ( usage %, latency, coverage )
- Renewal posture: green/amber/red + next touch date
- Top 3 asks (customer and vendor)

Standard track deck (recommended 8 slides, 20–30 min):
1) Cover + Agenda (1 slide) — include expected outcomes and decision requested (e.g., renewal approval, pilot expansion)
2) One-pager Snapshot (from above) — 1 slide, lead with value
3) Usage & Adoption Highlights (1 slide) — active users, routes, top models used, cost trends (token/unit)
4) Business Impact Stories (1–2 slides) — short customer quotes, specific product features used, success metrics (time saved, feature adoption %)
5) Health Signals & Risks (1 slide) — top three health indicators and actions; include support ticket trend sparkline
6) Roadmap & Opportunities (1 slide) — product features relevant to customer and potential expansions
7) Renewal Ask & Commercials (1 slide) — proposed term, pricing considerations, best alternative scenarios
8) Next Steps & Owners (1 slide) — commitments, deadlines, follow-up workshop dates

Enterprise track deck (recommended 14 slides + appendix, 40–60 min):
1) Cover + Governance roster (1 slide) — include escalation path and contacts
2) Exec Snapshot + Risk posture (1 slide)
3) SLA & SLO performance (1 slide) — uptime, median latencies, P99s, incidents in quarter
4) Traffic & Capacity Profile (1 slide) — concurrency, peak QPS, batch sizing, cost per 1M tokens
5) Model and Variant Matrix (1 slide) — models in production, quantization/precision, fallback map
6) Security & Compliance Summary (1 slide) — data flows, KMS/HSM usage, audit log highlights
7) Deployment Topology (1 slide) — diagrams for hosted/dedicated/private; call out network egress, VPC peering events
8) Observability & Incident Postmortems (1–2 slides) — recent incidents, mitigations, runbook changes
9) Cost Optimization Opportunities (1 slide) — batching/caching, quantization recommendations with estimated $ savings
10) Roadmap alignment & migration plan (1 slide) — compatibility windows for model upgrades, pinning strategy
11) Support & Escalation SLA (1 slide) — response/resolution targets and on-call rotations
12) Renewal commercial terms + custom options (1 slide)
13) Risk register & contingency plan (1 slide) — thresholds for failover to backup model/region
14) Action plan & sign-offs (1 slide)
Appendix: Deep diagnostics (KV cache hit rates, sample traces, console screenshots, raw usage tables)

Slide-level speaker notes (examples):
- Usage slide: "We saw a 37% increase in inference calls from Product Search route; prefix caching reduced mean latency by 45ms after deploy on Jan 12 — see page X for traces."
- SLA slide: "Two P1 incidents this quarter. Root cause: autoscaling misconfiguration on dedicated pool; mitigation: autoscaler tuning and pre-warm policy. Action owner: infra-SRE (Daniel Park)."

Renewal playbook (pre, during, post):
- Pre (30–45 days out):
  * Run renewal risk scan (automated notebook) to classify: usage trends, invoice anomalies, support volume, feature gaps.
  * Prepare tailored 1-pager: impact + 3 suggested commercial levers.
  * Align internal stakeholders: Sales, Legal (if enterprise), Solutions Eng.
  * Draft proposed term and walk-away date.
- During (QBR meeting):
  * Start with the one-pager, confirm meeting outcomes.
  * Surface the renewal posture & ask early (before deep dives) to secure alignment.
  * For enterprise: schedule a 20-min technical slot mid-meeting; capture technical open items live.
  * Agree on timeline for decision and any gating deliverables.
- Post (48–72 hours):
  * Send summary email with: recording, slide deck, decisions, owners, and updated renewal tracker row.
  * Create follow-up tasks in Jira/Linear for cross-functional work.
  * Trigger commercial handoff to renewals team if appropriate.

Renewal tracker (recommended columns for shared sheet):
- Customer name | ARR | Renewal date | Renewal posture | Last QBR date | Decision owner | Proposed TCV | Cross-sell opportunities | Technical risk level | Next milestone | Notes

Roles & responsibilities (suggested):
- CSM: lead the QBR, assemble deck, drive follow-ups
- Solutions Eng: technical appendix, SLO/SLA slides, postmortem summaries
- Account Exec: commercial ask, negotiation, pricing approvals
- SRE/Infra: incident summaries, capacity forecasting

Meeting planner checklist (for the CSM):
- [ ] Confirm stakeholders and send calendar invites with expected outcomes
- [ ] Run latest usage export from Console (attach sanitized charts)
- [ ] Validate health signals with Support inbox and Solutions Eng
- [ ] Prepare TL;DR one-pager and two alternate renewal scenarios
- [ ] Pre-read: send one-pager 3 business days before meeting

Sample invite subject lines and pre-read blurb (copy/paste):
- Subject: "QBR: Acme Inc — Q1 2026 (30 min) — Decision: Renew / Expand"
- Pre-read blurb: "Quick one-pager attached — we’ll cover adoption highlights, any technical risks, and finalize renewal next steps. Expect 30–45 minutes. Please add anyone from infra/SRE if you'd like the technical review.

Visual guidance & assets:
- Use console screenshots with timestamps and anonymized IDs.
- Include small sparklines for trends (usage, latency, tickets).
- Prefer bullet plain language vs. long paragraphs for exec slides.
- For Enterprise diagrams, use simple network boxes and annotate traffic volumes.

Common risks and mitigations (examples):
- Risk: Spiking token costs from burst routes. Mitigation: rate-limits + burst policy + revised per-route pricing.
- Risk: Latency degradation when moving to larger context windows. Mitigation: selective KV caching + longer-tail batching policy.

Templates included in repo (where to copy blocks from):
- exec-one-pager.md (short TL;DR block)
- enterprise-appendix-template.md (traces, cache rates, SLO table)
- renewal-email-templates.md (green/amber/red workflows)

Feedback loop:
- Please add comments in the linked GitHub PR for slide blocks you'd like added/removed. We’ll collect usage from the next 6 QBRs and update this slate in the January 2027 CS toolkit refresh.

Open questions to resolve before publishing final template:
- Do we want a separate legal checklist for every enterprise QBR or only when renewal moves to negotiation? (action: legal to weigh in)
- Should we include an optional "customer ask" slide where the customer lists top 3 product requests live in the meeting?

Next steps for this doc:
- Iterate with Sales and Solutions Eng by Mar 20 (owners: Maya + Daniel).
- Pilot with three enterprise accounts during Apr QBR cycle and collect outcomes.

Appendix (quick copyable checklist for after-meeting email):
- Subject: "QBR Recap & Next Steps — [Customer] — [Quarter]"
- Body bullets: 1) TL;DR decision posture 2) Key actions + owners + due dates 3) Proposed renewal commercial summary 4) Date for next check-in

End of draft.
